title: The guide's face promises a voice
statement: Show a guide's face or name only beside words the learner can actually hear, so a reader reaching for the audio is never offered a voice that doesn't exist.
detail: A younger-grade renderer shows the guide's avatar and name only beside text with real pregenerated audio, and any other line, including one the scorer writes at answer time, without a face. The reason given is that everything wearing the guide's portrait speaks, so the portrait tells a child which words have a voice behind them, and a face on unvoiced feedback offers a voice that does not exist to the child most likely to reach for it. The rules pair it with their read-along rule: nothing may be spoken that is not printed, and nothing may look spoken that cannot be.

evidence.quote: **Rule.** The guide's avatar and name appear only beside text the child can actually hear: a node with real pregenerated audio.
Any other line on the screen, including one written at answer time by the scorer, is shown without a face.
Everything in this app that wears the guide's portrait speaks, so the portrait is what tells a child which words have a voice behind them.
That rule says nothing may be spoken that is not printed.
This one says nothing may LOOK spoken that cannot be.
